title: RISE Live: the model changes the room
acceptance: Events: room.change is additive to rise.current-events.v1, one of visual.control {surface?, parameter, value} (a manifest command, as controlVisual takes one), scene.cue {scene, cue}, look.change {look} and pace.suggest {rate} (0.5 to 2), each bounded by the manifests and beats.js as a beat's cue is; the line format reads @visual, @cue, @look and @pace between beats, in a main stream or an interjection's answer.
The reducer admits them, anchored before the next beat; the sealed Current carries none.

The runtime applies a cue at once and every other change at a phrase boundary, one a phrase (a second waits for the next), where the model put it; what manifests, scenes or the reader's own settings refuse is a journal note (room.refused), never a stall (design §6, §8 stage 5: one visual, one phrase, one second).
A suggested pace applies only if the reader has not set a pace in this reading; the stage says RISE suggests it and the reader can refuse it.
The journal notes room.asked and room.changed; perception reports RISE's changes as RISE's, apart from the reader's; the room's persisted state (theme, intensity) follows.
REALTIME_INSTRUCTIONS teaches the room without orders: what each line does, when it is apt, and the restraint.

Demonstrated in the venue: a look and a cue mid-stream, an interjection answer that changes the visual, each landing at the next phrase boundary with the timings reported; a reader-set pace not overridden; the perception block names RISE's change.

evidence.note: §18 The model changes the room: the lines, the event, when a change lands, what each does, the reader's settings, perception, the guide, the demonstration, measurements and limits.
The model changes the room (added 2026-10-11, additive): room.change, its four kinds and bounds, EVENT_ROOM, ROOM_CHANGE, TOO_MANY_CHANGES.

Branch live-room-changes, the whole runtime on fake timers: a change lands at the start of the beat after its line, not when it arrives; one a phrase, a cue at once; an interjection's change at the answer's first beat within a second; refusals noted and the reading ends; the reader's intensity, theme and pace win; a suggested pace and the reader's way back. With protocol, stream, segment-parser, perception, openai-instructions, mock, stage-controls and LiveHost tests.

Branch live-room-changes, local production build, headless Chromium, the demo and the paced voice: look and cue landed 3 and 4 ms after the first phrase of the passage after them; the second change 1 ms after the next phrase began; an answer's change arrived 223 ms after the question and landed 438 ms later, 3 ms after the answer's first phrase; a reader-set pace refused RISE's (READER_SET); Keep 1× took a suggested pace back; the next question carried RISE's changes as RISE's.
Stage 5 (branch live-room-changes), stacked on #633 (base live-hardening). Open and held for the connector freeze: not merged, no auto-merge, not deployed.

Not by the coordinator: after answering Codex's one finding (aa93c705, Keep returns to the reader's own pace across successive suggestions), the Codex feedback workflow armed auto-merge, and with base live-hardening (no required check) #634 was squash-merged into live-hardening as 9aae06f4 on 2026-10-12. Nothing reached main: stage 5 now rides in #633, still open and held. A regression test for the finding was added after it.

Stage 5 rode in #633, merged as e0332586 and deployed: rise.syberlabs.io/release.txt read e033258683234305aebc4c4c54aa52252b3c9c76 on 2026-10-11 (the production job passed). Not accepted: no real model has written a room line.
